task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the smallest power of 2 greater than or equal to n.
specification_response:
method SmallestPowerOf2GreaterThanOrEqualTo(n: int) returns (result: int)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The returned value is a power of 2
    - The returned value is greater than or equal to n
    - The returned value is the smallest such power of 2 satisfying these conditions
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method NextPowerOfTwo(n: int) returns (power: int)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - n should be non-negative
    
Dafny specification:
    requires n >= 0
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The returned power is a power of 2 (i.e., has exactly one bit set)
- The power is greater than or equal to n
- The power is the smallest such power of 2 satisfying the above
    
Dafny specification:
    ensures power >= n
    ensures power != 0
    ensures (power & (power - 1)) == 0  // power is a power of two
    ensures forall p: int :: p >= n && (p & (p - 1)) == 0 ==> power <= p

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method NextPowerOfTwo(n: int) returns (power: int)
    requires n >= 0
    ensures power >= n
    ensures power != 0
    ensures (power & (power - 1)) == 0  // power is a power of two
    ensures forall p: int :: p >= n && (p & (p - 1)) == 0 ==> power <= p
{
    power := 1;
    while power < n
        invariant 1 <= power
        invariant power >= n || (power & (power - 1)) == 0
        invariant forall p: int :: p >= n && (p & (p - 1)) == 0 ==> power <= p
    {
        power := power * 2;
    }
}
```
